title: Cross-channel launch operational runway and KPI anchors
content:
Purpose and scope
---
This doc is a working operational runway and KPI anchor for a cross-channel feature launch (hosted API + Dedicated + Console). It focuses on the last-mile operational checks, metric guardrails, stakeholder ownership, and explicit rollback triggers. Use this as the authoritative pre-launch checklist for the product ops, SRE, and GTM teams until the release playbook is finalized.

High-level launch goals
---
- Deliver feature X to 3 phased cohorts (internal beta, early customers, public) with predictable latency and cost.
- Keep end-to-end success rate >= 99.5% for the early customer phase.
- Keep 95th percentile generation latency under 380ms for sample traffic profile.
- Maintain token cost delta <= +12% vs baseline model during rollout.

Release phases and gating summary
---
Phase 0 — Canary (internal): 5% internal traffic, 48h burn-in. Must pass smoke and production-like load tests.
Phase 1 — Early customers: 10–20 curated customers, 7 days. Close monitoring and weekly syncs.
Phase 2 — Graduated ramp: 25–75% for 72h windows with manual go/no-go decisions.
Phase 3 — Public: full traffic; fallback policy in place to prior stable variant and cross-region routing.

KPI anchors (operational) — definitions and targets
---
1) Availability (route-level) — successful request rate (2xx) excluding client errors: target >= 99.5% (per 24h). Owner: SRE oncall. Alert: >= 2% drop vs baseline for 30m.
2) Latency — p95 end-to-end (ingest->response): target <= 380ms for host-model-default. Owner: serving-runtime lead. Alert: sustained p95>450ms for 15m.
3) Cost per 1k tokens — unit cost delta vs baseline model: target <= +12%. Owner: finance & infra. Alert: > +20% sustained for 24h.
4) Quality regression — automated eval set pass rate (precision @k / rouge-like): decrease <= 3% vs control. Owner: applied-ml. Alert: >3% drop for 3 consecutive runs.
5) Error spectrum — rate of 5xx and model-timeout errors combined: target <= 0.3% of successful attempts. Owner: runtime team. Alert: >1% for 30m.
6) Customer-facing incidents — open P0s: target 0. Owner: product success. Alert: any P0 related to feature.

Metric collection plan and dashboards
---
- Primary dashboards: "Launch / Feature X Runway" in Console (tokenized metric panels: success rate, latency histograms, cost per token, model inference CPU/GPU saturation).
- Sampling: detailed request traces for 1% of requests with full input/output to the quality eval pipeline.
- Log retention: 14 days hot, 90 days cold.
- Ownership: product-ops sets the dashboard, SRE publishes runbook links.

Pre-launch checklist (operational, network, security)
---
- [ ] Certificate validation: certs for public endpoints verified and auto-refresh tested. Owner: infra.
- [ ] DNS TTL and rollback TTL set to 60s for first 24h. Owner: infra.
- [ ] Model pinning: confirm model version hashes are immutable for canary. Owner: serving-runtime.
- [ ] Rate limits/circuit breakers configured per-customer to avoid noisy neighbors. Owner: api-gateway.
- [ ] Cost guardrails: automated quota alerts tied to finance thresholds. Owner: billing.
- [ ] SLO burn-in tasks: synthetic load generators running for 24h with expected p95 and success rate. Owner: SRE.
- [ ] Telemetry hooks: sampling and tracing enabled with sample identifiers for cohort tagging. Owner: observability team.
- [ ] Audit logs and KMS access checks completed for Private deployments. Owner: security.

Staged rollbacks and decision tree (condensed)
---
If any of the following triggers are met, escalate and consider rollback options in this order:
Trigger A: availability drop >= 2% vs baseline for 30m + rising error rates.
Trigger B: p95 latency > 450ms sustained 15m AND increasing queue times.
Trigger C: quality regression >3% on automated eval set for 3 consecutive runs.
Trigger D: cost delta > +20% 24h.
Steps:
1) Triage window (15m): product-ops + SRE + runtime lead assess logs and mitigating changes (reduce concurrency, lower batch size, route to fallback variant).
2) Partial rollback: divert 50% of forwarding for the cohort to prior stable model variant and set canary to internal-only.
3) Full rollback: route cohort back to prior stable branch, open incident, run RCA.
Responsibilities and contact matrix
---
- Product-ops (Maya Patel): launch coordinator, runbook maintainer, daily status.
- Serving-runtime (Samir Venkataraman): model pin, runtime knobs, rollback execution.
- SRE (Ethan Liu): infra scaling, oncall, circuit breaker tuning.
- Applied ML (Rosa Hernandez): quality evals, prompt tests, regression signoff.
- GTM (Jenna Ortiz): customer comms and early customer outreach.
- Support (Rajiv Singh): escalation channel and incident updates.

Communication plan and cadence
---
- Daily 09:00 standup (first 3 days of each phase) with representatives from each team.
- Asynchronous updates in #launch-ops Slack thread with a single summary message at 17:00 PT.
- External comms: template for customer emails and status pages stored in linked Confluence page.

Quick smoke tests (run before canary flip)
---
1) Happy path: 50 synthetic requests with target prompt templates — check outputs for structural correctness and p95 latency.
2) Edge cases: 10 malformed inputs — confirm validation errors and no 5xx crashes.
3) Rate spike: short burst test (2x expected peak) to confirm horizontal autoscaling triggers and no throttling beyond configured rate limits.

Known risks & mitigations
---
- Risk: sudden model-induced cost spike due to prompt changes. Mitigation: cadence gating on prompt changes; disable prompts-wide rollout if cost per 1k tokens trend > +15%.
- Risk: noisy neighbor from dedicated pool. Mitigation: enforce per-tenant GPU reservations and stricter CQ thresholds.
- Risk: quality regressions that only appear for small cohorts. Mitigation: preserve 5% sample logging to offline eval pipeline and run expedited human-in-the-loop checks.

Postmortem and learning capture
---
- For any trigger that generated partial or full rollback, owner must file a short RCA within 72h and a follow-up playbook update PR.
- Product-ops will run a 1-week post-launch retro focusing on metrics drift, communication gaps, and tooling shortfalls.

Appendix: quick reference commands & tickets
---
- Rollback command (runtime): repoint routing policy to variant v-2025-10-21-stable: /infra/routing revert --variant v-2025-10-21-stable --cohort early-customers
- Canaries and labels: attach label launch:feature-x and cohort:{internal|early|grad} to all traces.
- Tickets to create before phase 1: PRODOPS-xxx (launch checklist), SRE-yyy (load test job), RUNTIME-zzz (model pin confirmation).

Notes to self / loose ends
---
- Confirm whether Dedicated early customers need private CA certificates (Rosa).
- Finalize cost alert thresholds with finance by 2025-11-10.
- Schedule a pre-launch dry run two weeks before canary date.
